title: hardening: VS Code under the protected profile connects to whatever daemon .moe/daemon.json names, with no spawn provenance (no JetBrains activationRefusal/RF03 parity)
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review; architect-bd1eb82d had flagged it in comment-bd7e8461.

Evidence at 28df02f7: under runtimeProfile(...) === 'protected', MoeDaemonClient.connect() → ensureDaemonRunning() starts nothing when .moe/daemon.json exists. getVerifiedDaemonInfo() then checks only the /health project identity (probeDaemonIdentity), and ws:// connects. Nothing checks that VS Code, or the IDE, started that pid from the extension's installed runtime. JetBrains refuses this case in doConnect via MoeDaemonSupervisor.activationRefusal → RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance (RF01) and offers the RF03 replacement.

Scenario: a protected (verified-local) project whose daemon was started from the repository's own packages/moe-daemon/dist, for example by `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js start` in a terminal or by a legacy seat's autostart. VS Code adopts that daemon: a repository-supplied runtime serves the protected session. That breaks RF05's rule that a project file may add a refusal but never an admission.

Node has no portable process start-time API, so the JetBrains (pid, startInstant) record does not port directly. Options: an owner-only spawn record keyed by pid plus a per-spawn nonce the daemon echoes on /health (the daemon reports it but cannot mint it, since the record lives outside the repository); or refuse any daemon this extension-host session did not spawn, with an explicit replace prompt as in RF03.
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile VS Code activates (connects to) a daemon only when it can prove that this extension, from its installed runtime, started that daemon, during this session or after a restart through an owner-only record outside the repository; otherwise it shows a fixed refusal and opens no WebSocket.

An unverified daemon is replaced only after an explicit, safe-default confirmation, and stopped only through the installed CLI's stop with a bounded wait (RF03 parity); a decline, a dismissal or a failure keeps the refusal.

LEGACY behaviour and the existing moe-vscode tests are unchanged; new tests cover verified, unverified, stale-record and declined cases, and `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits 0 on Linux and on Windows.
taskRails: Protected-profile state lives outside the repository, owner-only; a missing, unreadable or mismatched record fails closed to the refusal.
No caller-minted evidence: nothing the daemon or the repository reports about itself admits a daemon on its own.
reopenReason: Human "move from backlog": CQ-RF07 residual (VS Code protected profile daemon spawn provenance parity).
